mainTopic: Must ריבית be returned? רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן on 'וחי אחיך עמך', challenges from ברייתות, the idea that שומא מילתא היא, and רב ספרא's rule comparing our courts to non-Jewish courts.
overview: This amud asks whether a lender who took ריבית must give it back. רבי אלעזר says yes, from the פסוק 'וחי אחיך עמך': give it back so your brother can live. רבי יוחנן uses that פסוק for רבי עקיבא's teaching about two travelers with one jug of water, where your own life comes first. The גמרא then challenges רבי יוחנן from ברייתות. The first is about sons who inherit ריבית money and must return only a recognizable item, for their father's honor, in a case where he repented. The second calls ריבית lenders 'robbers' who must return what they collected. The גמרא tries to show this is a dispute between תנאים, based on the 'קום עשה' of רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. It then pushes that back: 'קום עשה' may mean tearing up the interest document, because appraisal (שומא) is significant. The witnesses listed in the משנה prove this. Finally, רב ספרא gives a rule: our courts order ריבית returned exactly where non-Jewish courts would collect it. אביי and רבינא test this rule with סאה בסאה and with a mortgage without deduction, and רבינא's challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's source: return it so he can live
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי אלעזר's proof that ריבית must be returned: the פסוק 'וחי אחיך עמך' means give the money back so your brother can live.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And your brother shall live with you' means: give the interest back to him, so that he can live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes giving the source for רבי אלעזר, who says ריבית is taken back by the court. He reads the פסוק 'וחי אחיך עמך' as a command to give the money back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר understands 'let your brother live with you' in money terms: a borrower who paid ריבית is missing money he needs to live. So the lender must return it. This is the reading רבי יוחנן will now have to explain differently.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And your brother shall live with you' (ויקרא 25:36)

phrases.english: "And your brother shall live with you."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:36. This פסוק is in the section about not taking interest.

phrases.english: Return it to him so that he may live.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחֵי אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ אַהְדַּר לֵיהּ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנֵיחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אלעזר's derivation, which began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that ריבית is taken back by the court
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 25:36, 'וחי אחיך עמך', read as 'give it back so he can live'

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן do with this verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן, who does not require returning ריבית, explains the פסוק 'וחי אחיך עמך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, what does he do with this פסוק, 'And your brother shall live with you'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן learns from the פסוק that רבי אלעזר just used. This question sets up the next step, where the גמרא gives רבי יוחנן's use of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no words of the תורה are extra. If רבי יוחנן does not learn 'return the ריבית' from this פסוק, he must use it to teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan, this verse "And your brother shall live with you"
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַאי וְחֵי אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side explains the פסוק used in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי יוחנן takes from 'וחי אחיך עמך', since he does not use it to require returning ריבית.

steps.title: Two travelers and one jug of water
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses the פסוק for רבי עקיבא's teaching: when only one person can survive on the water, the owner of the water drinks, because your life comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what a ברייתא teaches: Two people were walking on a road, and one of them had a jug of water. If both drink, both will die. If one drinks, he will reach a town. בן פטורא taught: Better that both drink and die, so neither one sees the other's death. Then רבי עקיבא came and taught: 'And your brother shall live with you' means your life comes before your friend's life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן uses 'וחי אחיך עמך' for a different lesson. It is the source for רבי עקיבא's rule that your own life comes before someone else's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads the word 'עמך' (with you) closely: your brother lives together with you, meaning your own life comes first. So the person holding the water drinks it. בן פטורא disagreed, saying both should share and die rather than one watch the other die. Since the פסוק is used for this, רבי יוחנן has no extra פסוק teaching that ריבית must be returned.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the פסוק) for a different teaching
A תנא who held both should drink and die

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא teaches from 'וחי אחיך עמך' that your own life comes before your friend's life. This is why רבי יוחנן does not learn the return of ריבית from this פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not about ריבית at all. The גמרא brings it only to show that רבי יוחנן uses the same פסוק for a completely different lesson.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a key source in הלכה for how to weigh one life against another when not everyone can survive.

phrases.english: He needs it for that which is taught in a baraita:
Two people who were walking on the road

phrases.aramaic: וּבְיַד אֶחָד מֵהֶן קִיתוֹן שֶׁל מַיִם,
phrases.english: and in the hand of one of them was a jug of water;
if both drink, they die,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם שׁוֹתֶה אֶחָד מֵהֶן – מַגִּיעַ לַיִּשּׁוּב.
phrases.english: and if one of them drinks, he reaches a settled area.
Ben Petora taught:
It is better that both drink and die,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יִרְאֶה אֶחָד מֵהֶם בְּמִיתָתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: and let one of them not see the death of his fellow.
Until Rabbi Akiva came and taught:
"And your brother shall live with you,"
your life comes before the life of your fellow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן uses the פסוק for רבי עקיבא's rule that your life comes before your friend's, so it is not available to teach returning ריבית.

steps.title: Challenge: the father must return the interest
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says sons who inherit ריבית money do not have to return it. This seems to mean that the father himself would have to return it, against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא challenges: If their father left them money from ריבית, even though they know it is ריבית money, they do not have to return it. This implies that their father would have to return it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's view that ריבית does not have to be returned. It points to a ברייתא that seems to assume the father does have to return it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא frees only the sons. The גמרא reads that as a hint: if the sons are free, then the father, who took the ריבית, must be obligated. That goes against רבי יוחנן, who says the lender is not forced to return it.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged: an objection from a ברייתא

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: הִנִּיחַ לָהֶם אֲבִיהֶם מָעוֹת שֶׁל רִבִּית,
phrases.english: If their father left them money of interest,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹדְעִים שֶׁהֵן שֶׁל רִבִּית –
phrases.english: even though they know that it is from interest,
they are not obligated to return it.
This implies that their father is obligated to return it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי הִנִּיחַ לָהֶם אֲבִיהֶם מָעוֹת שֶׁל רִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question about the פסוק and directly challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that ריבית is not taken back by the court
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא frees only the sons. That implies the father who took the ריבית must return it, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The father is free too; the wording follows the next clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the father really does not have to return the ריבית either. The ברייתא spoke about the sons only to match its סיפא, which is about the sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, their father does not have to return it either. But since the תנא wanted to teach the סיפא, 'If their father left them a cow, a garment, or any recognizable item, they must return it because of their father's honor,' he also taught the רישא about them, the sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge. The ברייתא's focus on the sons does not prove that the father must pay back the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא has a rule that applies only to sons: they must return a recognizable item for their father's honor. To keep both clauses parallel, the תנא also worded the רישא about the sons. So there is no hint that the father must return the money, and רבי יוחנן stands.

keyTerms.meaning: By right, really, the law is
Since, because (the wording was chosen to match)

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge falls away. The father is also not forced to return ריבית money, which fits רבי יוחנן. The sons must return only a recognizable item, and only because of their father's honor.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the sons must return the cow or garment because it is ריבית that must be returned. The reason the ברייתא gives is only their father's honor.

phrases.aramaic: בְּדִין הוּא דַּאֲבוּהוֹן נָמֵי לָא מִיחַיַּיב לְהַחְזִיר,
phrases.english: By right, their father too is not obligated to return it,
but since he wants to teach the latter clause:
If their father left them a cow or a garment
or any defined item,
phrases.notes: Something people would recognize as the item the father got wrongly.

phrases.english: they are obligated to return it because of their father's honor,
he also taught the first clause about them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the sons, so both halves of the ברייתא talk about the sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדִין הוּא דַּאֲבוּהוֹן נָמֵי לָא מִיחַיַּיב לְהַחְזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the ברייתא's wording as matching the סיפא, so no inference can be drawn about the father.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the ברייתא frees only the sons, the father must be obligated to return ריבית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father is also not obligated. The רישא was worded about the sons only to match the סיפא, which is a rule for sons alone (their father's honor).

steps.title: Why should the sons honor a father who took interest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the סיפא of the ברייתא: why must sons return an item to honor their father if he sinned by taking ריבית?
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these sons really obligated to act for their father's honor? The פסוק says 'do not curse a leader among your people', which teaches that we only honor someone who acts the way our people should act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the סיפא of the ברייתא from the last step, which made the sons return a known item because of their father's honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father who lent with ריבית did something wrong, so he is not 'acting like your people'. The פסוק suggests that such a person does not get the special respect. So why should his honor force the sons to return anything?

keyTerms.meaning: One who acts the way your people should act

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי, מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹד אֲבִיהֶם מִי מִיחַיְּיבִי?
phrases.english: And these sons, are they obligated because of their father's honor?
Read here: "And a leader among your people you shall not curse,"
which applies to one who acts the way your people act.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי, מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹד אֲבִיהֶם מִי מִיחַיְּיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the סיפא of the ברייתא that step 5 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's סיפא, which makes sons return an item because of their father's honor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sinner is not 'acting like your people', so his honor should not obligate the sons.

steps.title: The father did תשובה
steps.stepSummary: Using a teaching of רבי פנחס in the name of רבא, the גמרא says the case is where the father did תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי פנחס said in the name of רבא, the case is where he repented. Here too, the case is where the father repented.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the father regretted his sin, so he is again someone who acts like 'your people'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the father did תשובה, he is no longer seen as a sinner and deserves honor. So the sons' duty of כבוד אב applies again.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Pinchas said in the name of Rava:
it is where he repented;
here too, it is where he repented.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי פִּנְחָס מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father was still a sinner and not worthy of honor.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father did תשובה, so he deserves honor.

steps.title: If he repented, why did he still have the item?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the father truly repented, why was the ריבית item still with him?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he repented, what is the item still doing with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes at the answer: real תשובה would mean giving the item back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who truly regrets taking ריבית would return it. The fact that it was still in his hands seems to show his תשובה was not real.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it doing with him?

phrases.aramaic: אִי עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה, מַאי בָּעֵי גַּבֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: If he repented, what is it doing with him?
phrases.notes: "It" means the ריבית item the sons found among his things.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה, מַאי בָּעֵי גַּבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the father did תשובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real תשובה means returning the item, yet the item was still with him.

steps.title: He died before he could return it
steps.stepSummary: The father did repent, but he died before he managed to give it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not get a chance to return it before he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the father meant to return it, but death came first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the father was truly a בעל תשובה and deserves honor. The sons finish the job for him by returning the item.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not manage / did not have time

steps.whatToRemember: The sons return a known ריבית item only because of their father's honor, in a case where he repented but died before returning it.

phrases.english: Where he did not manage to return it before he died.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא הִסְפִּיק לְהַחְזִיר עַד שֶׁמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Keeping the item shows the תשובה was not real.
steps.terutzMaskana: He sincerely repented but died before he could return it.

steps.title: A ברייתא: robbers and interest lenders must return
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says robbers and ריבית lenders must return what they collected, against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: robbers and those who lend with interest, even though they already collected, must return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attack on רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא that seems to require returning ריבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said ריבית does not have to be returned. This ברייתא says lenders with interest must return what they collected, which sounds like the exact opposite.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Robbers and those who lend with interest,
even though they collected, must return it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַגַּזְלָנִין וּמַלְוֵי רִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge to רבי יוחנן after the previous one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that ריבית does not have to be returned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says ריבית lenders must return what they collected.

steps.title: The wording 'even though they collected' doesn't fit robbers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how 'even though they collected' could describe robbers.
steps.simpleTranslation: With robbers, what case is there of 'even though they collected'? If they robbed, they robbed. If they did not rob, would you call them robbers?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to understand the ברייתא's wording, because 'collected' is a strange word for a robber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A robber does not 'collect' money; he simply steals it. And if he did not steal, he is not a robber at all. So the phrase 'even though they collected' cannot really be about ordinary robbers.

phrases.aramaic: גַּזְלָנִים מַאי ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגָּבוּ״ אִיכָּא?
phrases.english: Robbers, what "even though they collected" is there?
If they robbed, they robbed;

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא גְּזוּל – גַּזְלָנִין קָרֵית לְהוּ?!
phrases.english: if they did not rob, do you call them robbers?!

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּזְלָנִים מַאי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגָּבוּ אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of the ברייתא brought in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'even though they collected' mean when talking about robbers?

steps.title: The 'robbers' are the interest lenders
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really means: robbers, meaning interest lenders, must return even what they collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: Robbers, who are they? Those who lend with interest. Even though they collected, they must return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא: 'robbers' is a description of the interest lenders. This makes the challenge against רבי יוחנן even sharper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls ריבית lenders 'robbers' and says they must return what they collected. That is a clear statement that ריבית must be returned, against רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rather, say: Robbers, who are they?
Those who lend with interest.
Even though they collected, they must return it.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not two groups (robbers and lenders). The word 'robbers' is just a description of the interest lenders themselves.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: גַּזְלָנִין, מַאי נִיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 11, completing the challenge of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Robbers' here means interest lenders, who must return ריבית even after collecting it.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this question is a מחלוקת between תנאים, and brings the view of רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב free the lender and the guarantor from lashes, because they have a 'get up and do' מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows some תנאים, while רבי יוחנן follows other תנאים. It brings a ברייתא to show which תנאים hold that ריבית is returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a לאו which can be fixed by doing a מצוה afterward does not get מלקות. These תנאים say the lender and guarantor get no מלקות for ריבית because there is something they can still do to fix it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
'Get up and do', an action that fixes the sin

phrases.english: It is a dispute between tanna'im, as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov
exempt the lender and the guarantor,
phrases.notes: They are free from lashes, even though they broke the לאו of ריבית.

phrases.english: because they have a "get up and do."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 10-12 by saying the ברייתא is only one side of a dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים: the ברייתא follows one view, רבי יוחנן follows another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the only view, so רבי יוחנן is contradicted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some תנאים hold ריבית must be returned, and רבי יוחנן can follow the ones who disagree.

steps.title: The 'get up and do' is returning the interest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the 'get up and do' must mean returning the ריבית, proving these תנאים require it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'get up and do'? Is it not that we tell them: Get up and give it back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what fixing action these תנאים meant, to prove that they hold ריבית must be returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only action that could fix the sin of ריבית is giving the money back. So these תנאים must hold that ריבית is returned, and the ברייתא of the 'robbers' follows them, not רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא proposes that whether ריבית must be returned is a dispute between תנאים, with רבי יוחנן following the תנא קמא. Step 16 will question this reading of 'קום עשה'.

phrases.english: What is the "get up and do"?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִינַן לְהוּ קוּמוּ אַהֲדוּרוּ?
phrases.english: Is it not because we say to them: Get up and return it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קוּם עֲשֵׂה? לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִינַן לְהוּ קוּמוּ אַהֲדוּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא of step 13 to prove that these תנאים require returning ריבית.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב hold ריבית must be returned
steps.raayaSupportSource: Their reason for no lashes, 'קום עשה', which must mean returning the ריבית

steps.title: So the first תנא holds interest is not returned
steps.stepSummary: From רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the גמרא infers that the תנא קמא holds ריבית does not have to be returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that the first תנא holds that these people are not obligated to return the interest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof. If רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב exempt from lashes because the money must be returned, then the תנא קמא, who does give lashes, must hold that there is no return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes are not given for a לאו that can be fixed by an action. So if the תנא קמא gives lashes, there must be nothing to fix, meaning no return of the ריבית. That would make רבי יוחנן's view the same as the תנא קמא's, so the question is a מחלוקת between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: the first, unnamed תנא in the ברייתא

phrases.english: By implication, the first tanna holds
that they are not subject to returning it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the proof begun in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That whether ריבית is returned is a מחלוקת between תנאים, with the תנא קמא agreeing with רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reason given by רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב for exempting from lashes: 'קום עשה'.

steps.title: No, 'get up and do' means tearing up the document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: 'קום עשה' may mean tearing up the interest document, not returning money.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What is the 'get up and do'? Tearing up the document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The fixing action that רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב mean might be tearing up the loan document, not giving back interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'קום עשה' means tearing the שטר, then nobody in the ברייתא is talking about returning ריבית. So we cannot infer that the תנא קמא holds ריבית is not returned. The attempt to show a מחלוקת between תנאים, which was meant to defend רבי יוחנן, is undercut.

keyTerms.meaning: 'get up and do', a positive action that fixes the sin
to tear up the loan document

phrases.english: No, what is the "get up and do"?
To tear up the document.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מַאי קוּם עֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 15 by reading 'קום עשה' differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that 'קום עשה' must mean returning ריבית.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed only one possible meaning of 'קום עשה'; tearing the שטר is another.

steps.title: What could tearing the document accomplish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading: whether or not a document counts as already collected, tearing it seems to fix nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he hold? If he holds that a document that stands to be collected is as if already collected, then they already did their sin. And if it is not as if collected, then they did nothing at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that tearing the document is the fix. It sets up two options and shows that tearing seems pointless under both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: the document counts as collected, so the sin is already complete and tearing it cannot undo it. Option two: the document does not count as collected, so no sin happened yet and there is nothing to fix. Either way, tearing does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: a document that is ready to be collected
it is treated as already collected

phrases.english: What does he hold?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא who says the fix is tearing the document.

phrases.english: If he holds that a document that stands to be collected
is as though it was collected,
then they already committed their sin.
And if it is not as though it was collected,
then they have not done anything at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר שְׁטָר הָעוֹמֵד לִגְבּוֹת כְּגָבוּי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that tearing the שטר is the 'קום עשה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: under either view of an uncollected document, tearing it neither undoes a finished sin nor fixes a sin that never happened.

steps.title: The document is not 'collected', but appraisal is significant
steps.stepSummary: The תנא holds the document is not treated as collected, but writing it still matters because it allows שומא, appraisal of the borrower's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he holds that a document that stands to be collected is not as if collected. And this teaches us that appraisal is a significant thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by choosing the second option and adding a new idea: a document that allows appraisal and collection is already a meaningful act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the money is not yet considered collected, writing the document counts as a real transgression, because it lets the lender appraise and seize the borrower's property. Since there is a real sin that can still be undone, tearing the document is a true fix.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually (keeping one side of the question)
appraisal of property in order to collect from it

phrases.english: Actually, he holds

phrases.aramaic: שְׁטָר הָעוֹמֵד לִגְבּוֹת לָאו כְּגָבוּי דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: that a document that stands to be collected is not as though it was collected,
and this is what it teaches us:
that appraisal is a significant matter.
phrases.notes: With this document the lender can have the borrower's property appraised and take it, so just writing it already counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר שְׁטָר הָעוֹמֵד לִגְבּוֹת לָאו כְּגָבוּי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the dilemma of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Chooses one side of the dilemma and adds a new principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the document is not treated as collected, nothing happened, so there is nothing to fix.
steps.terutzMaskana: The document is not treated as collected, but because it enables שומא, writing it is a real transgression that tearing it can fix.

steps.title: Proof from the witnesses in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה lists the עדים among those who violate the לאו of ריבית; since witnesses do nothing except enable appraisal, appraisal must be significant.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also reasonable, as we learned: These violate a negative commandment: the lender, the borrower, the guarantor, and the witnesses. It makes sense for all of them, since they did an action. But what did the witnesses do? Rather, learn from this that appraisal is a significant matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the idea that שומא מילתא היא. It uses a משנה that counts the witnesses as sinners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender, borrower and guarantor all take part in the loan itself. The witnesses only sign the document, and that signature is what makes appraisal and collection possible. If they are counted as transgressing, it must be because enabling appraisal is significant.

keyTerms.meaning: so too it is reasonable (a support for what was just said)

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable, as we learned in a mishna:
And these violate a negative commandment:
The lender and the borrower, the guarantor and the witnesses.
Granted, all of them did an action,
but the witnesses, what did they do?
Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this
that appraisal is a significant matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the principle stated in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: שומא מילתא היא, appraisal is a significant matter.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing the עדים among those who violate the לאו of ריבית.

steps.title: Conclusion: appraisal is significant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: שומא מילתא היא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the proof and closes this part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing an interest document is a real transgression, because it allows appraisal and collection. That is why tearing it can count as the 'קום עשה'. So the proof that the תנא קמא denies returning ריבית is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from this; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: 'קום עשה' can mean tearing up the interest document, because שומא מילתא היא. The witnesses in the משנה prove it. So the ברייתא does not show that the תנא קמא holds ריבית is not returned.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שומא מילתא היא: writing an interest document that enables appraisal is itself a real transgression, and tearing it is the fix.

steps.title: רב ספרא's rule: follow what non-Jewish courts would collect
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא says: if non-Jewish courts would collect the interest from the borrower, Jewish courts make the lender return it. If they would not collect it, Jewish courts do not make the lender return it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: In any case where, by their laws, one takes the money from the borrower and gives it to the lender, by our laws one returns it from the lender to the borrower. In any case where, by their laws, one does not take it from the borrower for the lender, by our laws one does not return it from the lender to the borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא gives a simple test for deciding when a lender must give back ריבית that he already took.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Non-Jewish law has no ban on interest, so it is a clear measuring stick. If their courts would enforce the deal as a real, binding obligation, our courts treat the payment as real ריבית and order it returned. If the deal is too weak or unclear for them to enforce, our courts do not order a return.

keyTerms.meaning: By their laws, meaning the laws of non-Jewish courts
They take out, meaning the court forces payment
They return, meaning the court forces the money to be given back

steps.confusionAlert: "Their laws" (דיניהם) means the laws of non-Jewish courts, which allow interest. It does not mean the laws of some other Jewish group.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule gives a working test for which kinds of ריבית a בית דין will actually force a lender to return.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
Any case where, by their laws,
phrases.notes: "Their laws" are the non-Jewish courts, which have no ban on interest.

phrases.english: one takes the money from the borrower for the lender,
by our laws one returns it from the lender to the borrower.
Any case where, by their laws,
one does not take it from the borrower for the lender,
by our laws one does not return it from the lender to the borrower.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא: כֹּל שֶׁאִילּוּ בְּדִינֵיהֶם מוֹצִיאִים מִלֹּוֶה לְמַלְוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of שומא to a practical rule for when ריבית is returned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jewish courts order ריבית returned exactly when non-Jewish courts would collect it.

steps.title: אביי challenges the rule from a loan of סאה בסאה
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether the rule always works. In סאה בסאה, non-Jewish courts would collect, yet our courts do not order the extra value returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Is this really a fixed rule? But there is the case of סאה בסאה, where by their laws one takes from the borrower for the lender, and yet by our laws one does not return it from the lender to the borrower!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב ספרא's rule by pointing to a case where it seems to fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In סאה בסאה, someone lends a measure of produce to be paid back with the same measure, and the price goes up in the meantime. Non-Jewish courts would make the borrower pay back the full measure, but our courts do not make the lender return the gain. So the rule "collect there means return here" seems to break.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed rule that always applies
Lending a measure of produce to be repaid with the same measure
But look at this case, which introduces a counterexample

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
And is this a fixed rule?
But there is the case of a se'a for a se'a,
phrases.notes: Lending a measure of produce to be paid back with a measure. If prices rise, the lender gains extra value.

phrases.english: where by their laws one takes it from the borrower for the lender,
and by our laws one does not return it from the lender to the borrower!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְלָלָא הוּא? וַהֲרֵי סְאָה בִּסְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ספרא's rule with a counterexample.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ספרא's claim that the rule works in every case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In סאה בסאה, non-Jewish courts collect, yet our courts do not order a return, so the two halves of the rule do not match.

steps.title: רב יוסף answers: non-Jewish law treats it as a deposit
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that in non-Jewish law the produce came to the borrower as a פקדון, not as a loan, so returning it is not paying interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In their view, it came into his hands as a deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends רב ספרא's rule by showing that סאה בסאה is not really a counterexample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Non-Jewish courts see the produce as a deposit that must simply be given back as it is. They are not collecting interest on a loan. Since they are not enforcing interest, the rule stays intact and our courts have nothing to return.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit: something held for its owner and returned as it is

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף answering אביי.

phrases.english: In their view, it came into his hands as a deposit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִינְהוּ בְּתוֹרַת פִּקָּדוֹן אֲתָא לִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: in non-Jewish law it counts as a deposit, not a loan with interest.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Non-Jewish courts collect interest in סאה בסאה, so the rule fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: They treat it as returning a deposit, so no interest is being enforced, and the rule holds.

steps.title: רבינא begins a challenge from a mortgage without deduction
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי about משכנתא בלא נכייתא, where non-Jewish courts would let the lender keep the field's produce. The challenge continues after this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But there is the case of a mortgage without deduction, where by their laws one takes from the borrower for the lender...
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא opens a new challenge to רב ספרא's rule with another case. The rest of the challenge comes next on the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In משכנתא בלא נכייתא, the lender holds the borrower's field and eats its produce without taking that value off the debt, which is a kind of interest. Non-Jewish courts would let the lender keep this. The challenge is being set up to show that our courts may treat it differently, which would break the rule again.

keyTerms.meaning: A mortgaged field held by the lender until the loan is repaid
A deduction: subtracting the produce's value from the debt

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But there is the case of a mortgage without deduction,
phrases.notes: The lender eats the field's produce without taking it off the debt, so the produce works like interest.

phrases.english: where by their laws one takes it from the borrower for the lender

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא בְּלָא נַכְיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a second counterexample to רב ספרא's rule is raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ספרא's rule that what non-Jewish courts collect, Jewish courts order returned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Non-Jewish courts enforce משכנתא בלא נכייתא, and the challenge is building toward showing that our courts may not order a return in this case.
